chunks: Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had three wives, then married two more women in a single contract. He consummated the marriage with one of them, then died.

He عليه السلام said: “If he consummated the marriage with the one whose name he mentioned first and named at the time of the marriage contract, then his marriage is valid; she must observe the waiting period, and she is entitled to inheritance. But if he consummated the marriage with the woman who was named and mentioned after mention of the first woman, then his marriage is invalid, she has no inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period.”

key_terms.النِّكَاحِ: marriage as a legal marital bond
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: the waiting period a woman must observe after separation or death
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: the inheritance due from the deceased spouse’s estate
key_terms.عَقْدَةٍ: the marriage contract by which the union is concluded

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man with four wives marries two more women in one contract and then dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a man who already had four wives and then attempted to marry two additional women in one contract. The ruling depends on which woman was named first in the contract: the first-named marriage is treated as valid if consummated, while the later one is invalid, though the woman still observes the 'iddah.

Hadith.4463 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who had three wives and then married two more women in a single contract. He consummated the marriage with one of them and then died.
Imam (as) said: "If he consummated the marriage with the woman whose name was mentioned first during the marriage contract, then his marriage is valid, and she must observe the waiting period ('iddah), and she is entitled to inheritance. However, if he consummated the marriage with the woman whose name was mentioned after the first woman, then his marriage is invalid, she is not entitled to inheritance, but she must observe the waiting period ('iddah).
